conviction_note: Porsche SE's Q3 statement is close to a mechanical restatement of numbers that are already out: VW's Q3 (29 Oct), Porsche AG's 9M (27 Oct) and its own 18 Sep ad-hoc that reset the FY guide. The only open lines are whether the -0.5 to +1.5bn guide is narrowed (small positive lean) and the size of another non-cash impairment, which this stock has ignored twice this year. So p_up sits at 51 and abs_move at 2.3 (the European 'guide reiterated' median); the realised move will mostly be VW and Porsche AG beta on the day.

already_public.what: Ad-hoc (MAR Art. 17), 18 Sep 2026 17:18 CEST: FY2026 adjusted group result after tax guide cut to -0.5bn to +1.5bn (was +1.5 to +3.5bn) after VW's forecast cut. Net debt guide of 4.7-5.2bn confirmed. VW's ~6bn Porsche goodwill impairment does not affect Porsche SE's results.
H1 2026: adjusted group result after tax 0.949bn, group result -2.218bn after impairments of 3.0bn (VW) and 0.2bn (Porsche AG), net debt 4.982bn, Quantum Systems revaluation +111m

VW Q3 2026 (the at-equity input, about 31.9% stake): Q3 operating result -5.86bn including a 6.4bn Porsche goodwill write-down, Q3 after-tax loss about -5.8bn, 9M after-tax -2.7bn, FY guide of up to 1% operating margin kept, further early-retirement restructuring expenses expected
Federal Court of Justice (BGH) dismissed the appeals in the KapMuG model case. The roughly 5.4bn of 2008-era damages claims fail and the ruling is final.
Porsche AG 9M 2026 results (the second at-equity input, about 12.5%)

new_in_release.expect: Confirmation of -0.5 to +1.5bn is the base case. A narrowing toward the upper half is possible because 9M adjusted should land near 1.0-1.1bn (H1 0.95bn plus a small positive Q3 VW contribution once the goodwill impairment is excluded). Direction slightly positive, small.
9M adjusted result about 1.0-1.1bn (my arithmetic, not a consensus); largely derivable from the VW and Porsche AG releases. No surprise expected.

Another non-cash impairment-test result on the VW and/or Porsche AG carrying amounts (Q1 -1.3bn, H1 -3.0bn cumulative on VW). Group result after tax likely deeply negative; the stock has looked through this before.
Net debt near 5.0bn, inside the 4.7-5.2bn guide; no change expected
unknown. Not normally addressed in a Q3 statement. VW's 9M loss threatens the 2027 dividend inflow, but that resolves in March 2027.

findings.finding: On VW's published Q3 (after-tax loss of about -5.8bn, of which the 6.4bn Porsche goodwill write-down does not reach Porsche SE's adjusted result), Porsche SE's 9M adjusted result should be about 1.0-1.1bn against an FY guide of -0.5 to +1.5bn. The guide's midpoint therefore implies a negative Q4, which leaves room to confirm or narrow upward rather than cut again.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 18 Sep 2026 ad-hoc guide cut moved PAH3 -3.38% on 21 Sep (VOW3 -2.01%). Earlier guide confirmations in quarterly statements moved +1.90% (11 Nov 2025, VOW3 +2.03%), -0.12% (13 May 2026) and +0.38% (7 Aug 2026), i.e. with VW.
findings.original_quote: Zu den Sondereffekten zählen eine nicht zahlungswirksame Abschreibung von 6,4 Milliarden Euro auf den Firmenwert von Porsche ... (Special items include a non-cash write-down of 6.4bn euros on Porsche goodwill.) Porsche SE ad-hoc, 18 Sep: 'The non-cash impairment of approximately 6 billion euros at the Volkswagen Group level does not affect either the adjusted group result after tax or the group result after tax of Porsche SE'
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: anyone can do this arithmetic from VW's 29 Oct release, and PAH3 has risen with VW since (+4.1% over 20d). What would remain unpriced is an explicit narrowing; if the market expected one, PAH3 would have outrun VOW3 since 29 Oct, and it has roughly tracked it (PAH3 25.16 to 26.23, VOW3 69.04 to 70.72 from 28 Oct to 9 Nov, Yahoo).
findings.independence: H1 adjusted 0.949bn from Porsche SE's own release (https://www.porsche-se.com/en/media/press-releases/detail/porsche-se-calls-for-swift-action-at-volkswagen-to-improve-competitiveness); the 9M estimate is my inference combining that with VW's Q3

findings.finding: Porsche SE runs impairment tests every quarter: Q1 -1.3bn on VW, H1 -3.0bn on VW and -0.2bn on Porsche AG. VW's Sept forecast cut and Q3 loss make another non-cash write-down in Q3 likely, which would push the group result after tax deeper into loss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (-1.3bn impairment): -0.12% on 13 May. H1 2026 (-3.0bn): +0.38% on 7 Aug (VOW3 +1.01%). The FY2024 -20bn result was ad-hoc'd ahead and the release days were flat.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced as irrelevant: impairments are non-cash, the adjusted result and net debt exclude them, and the stock trades on look-through NAV. A market that cared would have sold PAH3 on the two earlier impairment days, and it did not.

findings.finding: The 30 Sep BGH ruling ended the roughly 5.4bn KapMuG claims for good. The Q3 statement is the first periodic report since then and may record the end of the litigation risk (and any release of legal-cost accruals).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ruling day 30 Sep 2026: PAH3 +1.15% against VOW3 -0.82%, a relative +2.0 points, so it was priced on the day
findings.why_not_priced: Already priced: it was public on 30 Sep and the stock outperformed VW by about 2 points that day. The only unpriced residue is a possible P&L effect, and I found no evidence that a provision exists (the H1 report PDF did not decode).

outside_window.finding: VW's 9M after-tax loss of -2.7bn threatens VW's FY2026 dividend, which is Porsche SE's main cash inflow (about 0.83bn from VW in 2026). Porsche SE's own dividend proposal is due with the FY results in March 2027.

baseline_tension: Neither agrees nor disagrees: the lean (-0.21, run-up driven) and the +4.1% 20-day run-up both reflect the VW recovery since 29 Oct, and nothing found is company-specific enough to stand against them.
language_note: The German press (web.de / auto-motor-und-sport, ORF) carried the VW Q3 special-item breakdown (6.4bn Porsche goodwill, about 1bn China, Osnabrück) that sets how much of VW's loss reaches Porsche SE's adjusted result; English snippets carried the same totals.
ORF's German report gave the timestamp that settles the session (published before the Xetra open on the H1 release day).
Otherwise nothing the English sources did not already carry: Porsche SE publishes everything bilingually (the German Finanzkalender matches the English one).
lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the BGH-ruling finding cut from +0.1 to +0.05, and the guidance finding from +0.2 to +0.15, because the 9M number is derivable from VW's public release.

'The move is in the guide' (reiterated or none: median 2.3%): abs_move_pct raised from 2.0 to 2.3. This name's own release-day history (median about 0.9%, tracking VW) is used for p_up only, not to cap the size.

'A German ad-hoc filed before the print may have pre-released the number': confirmed. The 18 Sep Prognoseanpassung is in already_public, and the findings are about what is left (narrowing, impairment).
